_strings.@@a64fd1bce23a: Treaty conformity — CT does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by CT. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: CT's resident return (Form CT-1040) starts from federal AGI (Line 1 = "Federal adjusted gross income from your 2025 federal income tax return"), so treaty-exempt income is initially excluded. HOWEVER, CT has an EXPLICIT ADD-BACK: the 2025 CT-1040 instructions (Schedule 1 additions, Line 37 "Other") and the 2025 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Schedule 1 additions, "Other") both direct, verbatim and unchanged from 2023 and 2024: "1. Add back any treaty income reported on federal Form 1040NR if a nonresident alien. Enter the words 'treaty income' in the space provided." Because CT requires nonresident aliens to add federally treaty-exempt income back into Connecticut adjusted gross income, CT does NOT conform to federal treaty exemptions for affected filers (analogous to California's Schedule CA add-back). Reinforcing this, the DRS Tax-Information page states that nonresident aliens who are domiciled in Connecticut, or who keep a permanent place of abode there and spend more than 183 days in the state, "are considered Connecticut residents even if federal Form 1040NR is filed for federal income tax purposes." Note: the add-back is scoped to nonresident aliens filing federal Form 1040NR; a filer with no treaty income is unaffected, but the statutory rule re-taxes treaty income, so conforms_to_federal_treaties = false.
_strings.@@c0e7931c928a: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Qualifying Jurisdictions (Schedule 2) — Connecticut residents (and part-year residents) whose income reported on the CT return is also subject to income tax in another qualifying jurisdiction (another U.S. state, a local jurisdiction within another state, or the District of Columbia) where the taxpayer filed a return and paid income tax. Prevents double taxation of the same income. A copy of the other jurisdiction's return must be attached.

Cannot be claimed if Form CT-1040 Line 10 is zero, cannot be carried forward, and is not refundable — "This credit can be used to offset only your 2025 income tax."

Computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule (2025 CT-1040 instructions, p. 19): Line 1 = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040, Line 5); Line 2 = Table A personal exemption; Line 3 = 'Connecticut Taxable Income: Subtract Line 2 from Line 1. If less than zero, enter 0.'; Line 4 = Table B Initial Tax Calculation (the rate schedules this block ships); Lines 5-6 add Table C (2% Tax Rate Phase-Out Add-Back) and Table D (Tax Recapture); Lines 8-9 apply the Table E personal-credit decimal; Line 10 'Connecticut Income Tax: Subtract Line 9 from Line 7. Enter here and on Form CT-1040, Line 6.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2025 RATES UNCHANGED — the TY2024 cut HELD: the 2024 reduction of the bottom two rates (3% -> 2% and 5% -> 4.5%, Connecticut's first income-tax rate cut since the mid-1990s) was NOT changed again for 2025. Table B for 2025 is digit-identical to TY2024 in every bound, rate and printed constant, and the DRS reprints the same four worked examples. Tables A, C, D and E are likewise unchanged from 2024 (Table C maxima still $250/$500/$250/$400; Table D still begins at CT AGI over $105,000/$210,000/$168,000 with maxima $3,400/$6,800/$5,320). Base guidance: supply Tax Calculation Schedule Line 3 (Connecticut Taxable Income) = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040 Line 5 = federal AGI + Schedule 1 additions - Schedule 1 subtractions) MINUS the Table A personal exemption. The Table A exemption (up to $15,000 single / $24,000 MFJ-QSS / $12,000 MFS / $19,000 HoH — unchanged for 2025) is INCOME-DEPENDENT — it falls $1,000 for each $1,000 (or part) of CT AGI over $30,000 / $48,000 / $24,000 / $38,000 and is $0 at CT AGI of $44,000 / $71,000 / $35,000 / $56,000 or more — so it is NOT shipped as a key; compute Table A on the form. At or above the zero point, Line 3 = CT AGI. Do NOT supply raw federal AGI when CT modifications apply, and do NOT subtract the exemption twice. Adjudication note (two-pass): drafted from the 2025 CT-1040 instructions (Rev. 12/25) Tables A-E and independently re-verified against the 2025 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Rev. 12/25) — Table A (221 numeric tokens), Table C (136) and Table D (450) compare as digit-identical multisets, all 28 Table E rows match row-by-row, and all 21 Table B rows match; zero discrepancies. Every printed '$X plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constant in Table B equals the EXACT cumulative sum of the prior brackets (200/2,000/4,750/10,750/14,000/31,250 single-MFS; 400/4,000/9,500/21,500/28,000/62,500 MFJ-QSS; 320/3,200/7,600/17,200/22,400/50,000 HoH), so pure marginal accumulation reproduces Table B to the half-dollar; the only divergence is IRS half-up rounding of a trailing $.50, and the DRS's own printed examples round the same way ($2,500 x .045 = $112.50 shown as $113 at MFJ Line 3 $22,500 -> $513, and $25,000 x .0699 = $1,747.50 shown as $1,748 at single Line 3 $525,000 -> $32,998). CRITICAL — Table C 2% Phase-Out Add-Back NOT modeled: if CT AGI (Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1, NOT taxable income) exceeds $56,500 single / $100,500 MFJ-QSS / $50,250 MFS / $78,500 HoH, Line 5 ADDS BACK $25-to-$250 in $25 steps (single, maximum above $101,500), $25-to-$250 (MFS, maximum above $72,750), $50-to-$500 (MFJ-QSS, maximum above $145,500), or $40-to-$400 (HoH, maximum above $114,500), clawing back the benefit of the 2% bottom rate. Plain bracket math (this op) UNDERSTATES the filed tax by the Table C amount — compute Line 5 on the form. Bands and amounts are identical to 2024. CRITICAL — Table D Tax Recapture NOT modeled: recapture begins at CT AGI over $105,000 single/MFS / $210,000 MFJ-QSS / $168,000 HoH, recapturing the 4.5%-rate benefit in $25/$50/$40 steps to a first plateau of $250/$500/$400 at CT AGI $150,000-$200,000 / $300,000-$400,000 / $240,000-$320,000, then a second phase in $90/$180/$140 steps to a plateau of $2,950/$5,900/$4,600 (single at CT AGI $345,000-$500,000; MFJ-QSS $690,000-$1,000,000; HoH $552,000-$800,000), then a third phase in $50/$100/$80 steps to the maximum $3,400 (single/MFS, over $540,000), $6,800 (MFJ-QSS, over $1,080,000), $5,320 (HoH, over $864,000). Plain bracket math understates the filed tax by the Table D amount — CT's Tax Calculation Schedule is the filed method. All 450 Table D numeric tokens are unchanged from 2024. Table E Personal Tax Credits NOT modeled (a TAX CREDIT, not a base reduction): a CT-AGI-keyed decimal (.75 down to .01 in 28 steps) multiplies the Line 7 tax and is subtracted on Line 9 for low/moderate incomes — e.g. .75 for single CT AGI over $15,000 up to $18,800 — fully phased out above CT AGI $64,500 single / $100,500 MFJ-QSS / $52,500 MFS / $78,500 HoH (identical to 2023 and 2024). No-tax floor (2025 CT-1040 instructions, Line 6): 'For each filing status, if the amount on Line 5 is: $12,000 or less for married filing separately; $15,000 or less for single; $19,000 or less for head of household; or $24,000 or less for married filing jointly, or qualifying surviving spouse, enter 0 on Line 6. You do not owe any income tax.' This coincides with the full Table A exemption at those AGI levels (the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches). Tax tables are OPTIONAL, not mandated: at CT AGI of $102,000 or less the filer 'may use the Tax Tables on the DRS website at portal.ct.gov/DRS/DRS-Forms/Current-Year-Forms/Calculators-and-Tables'; above $102,000 the filer may use the myconneCT Income Tax Calculator or the Tax Calculation Schedule. The Tax Calculation Schedule is the universal filed method at any income (table bands can differ from schedule arithmetic by a few dollars). One Table B schedule covers 'Single or Married Filing Separately' — duplicated for both statuses here, copied, not derived (Table A/C/E amounts DO differ between single and MFS). The MFJ schedule is titled 'Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse', so qualifying surviving spouse maps exactly to married_filing_jointly as the engine assumes. Connecticut has no county or municipal income taxes and no standard deduction; the Table A personal exemption and the Table E personal credit are the only general-relief mechanisms, both income-dependent, both computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule. The CT EITC (Line 20a) was expanded for 2025 — still 40% of the federal EIC, plus an additional $250 for a taxpayer with at least one federal qualifying child — but it is a refundable payment/credit applied after Line 6 and is not part of this block. Schedule 1 subtractions are the caller's, not this block's — the 2025 face adds Line 48d "Achieving Better Life Experience (ABLE)", summed into Line 50 and Line 4. 2025 Instructions p. 10, Line 48d ABLE (Achieving a Better Life Experience) Account: "Subtract the amount of your contributions made to an ABLE (Achieving a Better Life Experience) account. The modification cannot exceed the maximum allowable contribution. The maximum ABLE contribution that may be subtracted is the lesser of (1) the amount of contributions to all ABLE accounts during the taxable year; or (2)(A) $5,000 for each individual taxpayer, including individuals whose filing status on their Connecticut income tax return is single, head of household, filing separately, or (B) $10,000 for individuals whose filing status on their Connecticut income tax return is filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse." The booklet prints no statute, effective year, carryforward or beneficiary rule, and is silent on whether the account must be Connecticut's. (Schedule CT-IT Credit Line 3 "ABLE Account Tax Credit" is a different item — an employer credit.) Line 1 of the 2025 face cites "federal Form 1040, Line 11a, or federal Form 1040-SR, Line 11a" (the TY2025 Form 1040 prints AGI on 11a); Line 13 "Total allowable credits from Schedule CT-IT Credit, Part 1, Line 10" (2023: Line 11). The page-1 "Do you need health coverage?" box has no tax effect: 2025 Instructions p. 2, "By checking the box on Form CT-1040, Connecticut Resident Income Tax Return, you authorize the Department of Revenue Services to transmit certain demographic information about you and your household to Access Health CT. This election authorizes Access Health CT to contact you with information about health coverage options and financial assistance that may be available to you." — an authorization, so it is checked only when the filer asks for it.
